phases.name: Houselisting & Housing Census
phases.purpose: To create a systematic national inventory of all structures, houses, and living conditions, and to assess the standard of living of households across India.
phases.timing: Conducted typically 6 to 9 months prior to the population count (as per state notifications).
keyFocus: Building material (roof, wall, floor)
Use of census house (residence, shop, workshop, school)
Condition of the house (good, livable, dilapidated)
Household size and number of dwelling rooms
Ownership status of the house (owned, rented, any other)
Major source of drinking water and location
Source of lighting (electricity, solar, kerosene, etc.)
Access to latrine and drainage connectivity
Availability of kitchen and type of cooking fuel (LPG, PNG, firewood)
Availability of assets (radio/transistor, television, internet access, computer/laptop, telephone/mobile, bicycle, scooter/motorcycle, car/jeep/van)

phases.name: Population Enumeration
phases.purpose: To count every individual residing in India and collect demographic, social, cultural, and economic characteristics of each person.
phases.timing: Conducted nationwide during the designated enumeration window.
keyFocus: Full name and relationship to head of household
Sex (Male, Female, Other) and Date of Birth / Age
Current marital status and age at marriage
Scheduled Caste (SC) / Scheduled Tribe (ST) status
Religion and Mother Tongue / Other languages known
Literacy status and highest educational attainment
Economic activity, category of work, and main/marginal worker status
Occupation, industry, and class of worker
Place of birth and place of last residence (migration origin & reason)
Duration of stay at current residence
Fertility indicators (for ever-married women: children surviving, children born alive)

selfEnumerationStep.title: Digital Self-Enumeration Window
selfEnumerationStep.description: Before an enumerator visits your home, households can log in to the official Census India portal using their mobile number, complete the questionnaire online, and receive a Self-Enumeration Acknowledgment Number (SEAN). When the enumerator visits, you simply share your SEAN to quickly verify your household.
